meta.title: The M1 Classroom
meta.textType: story: a first look at the M1 building

paragraphs: On Friday, May seventh, at nine o'clock, the M one Open Morning started at the school gate. Nobody wore a school uniform, because the school was on holiday. Sam was twelve, and he was in M one. He led Lily, Mia, Leo, and May into the M one building. The cafeteria was on the ground floor, with long tables and a big window. "The cafeteria opens at noon," Sam told them. "Now you may go first," he said. "Go up the stairs, turn left, and the third door on the right is our classroom." Lily counted twenty-two steps and held the strap of her bag. They turned left past a long wall of lockers. The third door on the right had a small sign with the room number. "That is it," said Sam. Lily asked only small questions on the way, such as "Where do we leave our shoes?" Then she asked, "Which door is the lab?" Sam looked at her hand on the strap. "I felt the same last year," he said, and he took them to the lab door.

The science lab had long tables and a big poster on the wall. The poster said, "Water freezes at zero degrees and boils at one hundred degrees." Under it, one more line said, "In a freezer: minus eighteen degrees." "What does minus mean?" asked Leo. May looked at the numbers and said, "It means below zero." "So a freezer is eighteen degrees below zero," said Mia.

In the corridor, a board showed the rules of M one. Leo stood next to it and pointed at each line. "No earrings," he read. "No headphones in class. Phones off in class." "Walk on the left of the stairs." Mia pointed at her ear and said, "An earring is a small ring for the ear." Sam smiled. "You may keep headphones in your bag," he said, "but you may not use them in class."

Then they went into the classroom. The furniture was new, with wooden desks and a green board. A bookshelf stood in the corner, and a big fan hung from the ceiling. "Every subject has a different teacher," Sam told them. "We have science, math, and language lessons," he added. "Will it be hard?" asked May. "It may be hard at first," said Sam, "but you might like it."

Lily sat at a desk and put her bag on the floor. "The lab smelled like an old shoe," said Leo. "I think that the shoe is still inside the lab." Lily laughed, and her hand was not on the strap anymore.
